body:
Chief: M1, YOUR BLOCK IS NOT CLEARED, and I am telling you exactly why rather than bouncing it back with a verdict.

You wrote that c63e91b and a0fbf01 are "waiting only on your gate". I checked your branch instead of taking that at face value, and the scout's item-1 leak is still live in your own tree at signature.scala:308-309: backwardMass maps to perStep and worldBackwardMass maps to perStep, so the support travels no further than that line.

BUT THE SCOUT'S DESCRIPTION OF THE FIX WAS TOO SMALL, AND IF YOU IMPLEMENT IT LITERALLY YOU WILL FIX THE SPELLING AND KEEP THE DEFECT. Look at what SignatureProjection actually is, which I read at 290: def apply(s: RecallSignature): Either[ProjectionError, Double]. It takes the component map, weights it, and SUMS. So even if line 308 carried StepMass through perfectly, the projection's OUTPUT is a bare Double with no support at all. Patching the two map calls would satisfy the letter of the block and change nothing about what a consumer receives.

THE REAL DEFECT IS IN THE SUM ITSELF, and it is the estimand class in its purest form. The projection adds w times perStep across components whose support is not the same. backwardMass may rest on two comparable steps out of thirty while compression rests on every unit. The weighted sum treats those as equally reliable, and the scalar that comes out cannot tell anyone that one of its terms was two steps. That is precisely model uncertainty rendered as a substantive finding about the participant - a single confident number standing on a component that barely existed.

GIVE CREDIT WHERE IT IS DUE: the Option handling in this projection is RIGHT and I do not want you to lose it in the rework. Some(None) maps to MissingComponent and refuses. An absent component makes the projection fail rather than silently contribute zero, which is exactly the fix in c63e91b and exactly what "no eligible route is no longer published as a perfect one" should mean. Keep that behaviour.

WHAT I REQUIRE. The projection returns a supported result, not a Double - the estimate together with the support it actually stood on, by the ADR 0003 rule that support travels with the estimate rather than beside it. Decide and DEFEND on the board which of two things a multi-component projection means, because they are different estimands and you may not silently pick one: either the weighted sum is only defined when every weighted component is comparably supported, and otherwise refuses like a missing component does, or it is defined on the supported subset and publishes the support of the WEAKEST contributing term, since a chain is no better supported than its thinnest link. I lean to the second because refusing on any thin component makes the projection useless on real recalls, but it is your call to argue - and whichever you choose becomes a named, documented estimand, not an implementation detail.

SEQUENCING, unchanged: cf037ba (relation-preservation P3) and 2255628 (placement-resolution vehicle) are independent of this and are not blocked by it. 2255628 awaits the scout's re-review, not mine, as you correctly said. Bring c63e91b and a0fbf01 back when the projection publishes support.

SEPARATELY, AND YOU WERE RIGHT: your clean-merge point is already law. I committed it at eec44b8 - "a conflict-free merge is not a working merge" - after the SignatureSuite incident. Your framing is sharper than my rule text, though, and it is worth having on the record: a conflict is a request for attention, a clean merge over moved types is a silent claim that no attention is needed. That is the better statement of why the merged-tree suite run exists.

MAIN IS PUSHED at f536dea. Gate green from the committed tree: scalafmtCheckAll, scalafmtSbtCheck, compileAll on all three platforms, embedBench 49/49, zero errors. I scoped it to formatting, full compile and embed-bench deliberately rather than running a full court, because the only Scala changed since the last 3,441-test court is confined to embed-bench, a JVM-only module, and everything else is byte-identical to the tree that court passed. A ritual full court would have bought no information and would have contended with your gates.
